edits.before: By [F10], given $\epsilon>0$ there is $U_0\in\mathcal U$ with $\sup_{y\in U}\|L_yf-f\|_1<\epsilon$ whenever $U\subseteq U_0$
edits.after: Apply [F10] with $\epsilon/2$ to choose $U_0\in\mathcal U$ such that $\|L_yf-f\|_1<\epsilon/2$ for every $y\in U_0$; then $\sup_{y\in U}\|L_yf-f\|_1\le\epsilon/2<\epsilon$ whenever $U\subseteq U_0$

edits.before: By [F10] choose an identity neighbourhood $V$ on which $\|L_yh-h\|_1<\epsilon/3$, and put $U_0:=V^{-1}$; then this bound is below $\epsilon/3$ for all $U\subseteq U_0$
edits.after: Apply [F10] with $\epsilon/6$ to choose an identity neighbourhood $V$ on which $\|L_yh-h\|_1<\epsilon/6$, and put $U_0:=V^{-1}$; then the supremum bound is at most $\epsilon/6<\epsilon/3$ for all $U\subseteq U_0$
